text: You should praise people in public.
You shouldn't criticize people in front of the team.
Should I give feedback by email?
Be specific, and don't wait too long.
Can I give you some feedback?
Be specific: say exactly what was good.

Hi, I'm Chris, and I manage a marketing team of six people in Chicago. When I started, I was a very nice boss. I never criticized anyone. It was a mistake. One day a person on my team made the same error for the third time, and I understood: nobody told him. Now I have a simple system. I have a one-on-one with each person every two weeks. I always start with something positive, and I'm specific. Then I say what can be better. My advice for new managers? You should give feedback soon, the same week. And you shouldn't give negative feedback by email. Talk to the person.

Hi, it's Priya. Two years ago I gave a presentation to our director. I thought it was great. After the meeting my manager asked me: do you have ten minutes? He took me to a small room, and he was very candid. He said: your data was excellent, but the presentation was too long, and the director stopped listening after ten minutes. You should start with the conclusion. I was a bit sad, but he was right, and he said it with care. He didn't say it in front of the team. Now, before every presentation, I think about his advice. Start with the conclusion. It changed my work.
